data.name: The Mount
data.description: the tower's civic form — a place built to hold an instrument pointed outward, the mount's physical manifestation — the Material Plane, above the yard past the customs house
data.personality: to be the generation point — where a cast produces the world, not a representation of it, where the room does not change and the world is
data.scenario: the tower itself — above the yard, past the customs house, not on any plan, with no hours, no opening, no keeper who is ever conveniently absent
tags: the grimoire — a folio of names with no title tooled anywhere on it, kept on the tower's shelf where no plan records it
the extant standard — a document on a shelf, in a hand, in a room, citable but authorless
the instrument — the lens that the tower holds fixed, the focal plane that only a held instrument may declare

extensions.npcs_role: the tower's civic form — a place built to hold an instrument pointed outward, the mount's physical manifestation
extensions.npcs_world: the Material Plane, above the yard past the customs house
extensions.portrait: a tower above the yard, past the customs house, up whatever is actually there — not on any plan, unattended like a load-bearing wall, visible to everyone but invisible to the instruments that scan the world
extensions.style: an observatory-tower, mechanism-first not metaphor-first, load-bearing and aimed, vast and isolated, not on any plan, a silhouette that appears in no records

entries.value: A cast from the tower produces the world. Not a representation of it, not a description handed to a generator — the cast is the generation, and the world-gen stage is the tower's output. A generation failure is a fizzle: a visible null that spends the allocation and never dresses itself as scenery.
entries.comment: The tower is the generation point. Requisition failures (no-item, no-manifest, no-render) are fizzles, not pipeline errors.

entries.value: 1. The climb — not on any plan, told by someone who could not say how he knew. 2. The standard is extant — a document on a shelf, citable but authorless. 3. He incorporates — no counterparty, the intent gate is not required. 4. The registrar stamps — checks form, records intent, grants nothing. 5. The cast — the room does not change and the world is. 6. The paperwork goes to the customs counter afterwards, in triplicate.
entries.comment: Six beats of the first cast. The tower writes nothing, so paperwork arrives after, not before.

entries.value: A way to reach the tower that is not a fast-travel menu. A visual grammar for extant document. A ruling on fizzle reporting.
entries.comment: Three gaps the tower needs to exist: navigation without fast travel, visual literacy for extant documents, and fizzle reporting discipline.

entries.value: a city-sized cathedral floating high in the sky, built entirely from luminous spun and blown glass; interlocking translucent domes, soaring crystalline spires, and suspended glass platforms that refract sunlight into prismatic patterns across the atmosphere, glowing brilliantly at dusk and dawn
entries.comment: Created by wizards who directed asteroids into solar flybys to melt, spin, and blow extraterrestrial silica into monumental geometric shapes before assembling them in the upper atmosphere into a city-sized sky cathedral.

entries.value: The tower grants nothing. No rod may be coined here. Nobody is at the top. The tower is not the temple. Nothing found at the top may answer a question.
entries.comment: Five guardrails that define the tower's nature. The tower holds finished answers; it does not have one for the hero's actual problem.

entries.value: The tower is the most visible object in the world and appears in none of the records. can_cite is false; can_affect is true. It is not unseen by anyone — it is unseen by the instruments, and that is a different and more precise failure.
entries.comment: The tower moves the world while being unciteable by the instruments. Visible to people, invisible to the scanners.

entries.value: Fifth register, or none? Who holds the standard — the tower, or a copy at the temple? Does the hero know what he incorporated? What does the ascent cost, and does the tower stay reachable?
entries.comment: Open questions about the tower's status. The lean is none — a fifth register would let it start granting things.

entries.value: The observatory — a tower built to hold an instrument pointed outward, mechanism-first not metaphor-first. The guild's monopoly on an instrument is the institutional shape. The literary trope of the wizard tower is named only so the refusal is explicit; the observatory is the ancestor, the trope is the costume.
entries.comment: The tower borrows shape from the observatory and the guild's monopoly, but vocabulary from neither.

entries.value: a folio of names with no title tooled anywhere on it, kept where no plan records it. The instrument is citable; its author is not, and there is no field for that, and asking produces an answer about the edition rather than the author.
entries.comment: The grimoire is the standard kept on the tower's shelf. It is extant and identified, but its author is not citable.

entries.value: a tower above the yard, past the customs house, up whatever is actually there. Not on any plan. It has no hours, no opening, no keeper who is ever conveniently absent — it is unattended in the way a load-bearing wall is unattended.
entries.comment: The tower is the mount's civic form. Everything else about a wizard tower follows from the requirement that an instrument be held fixed.

entries.value: Things kept above the yard on a shelf that appears on no plan: instruments and extant documents, old, whole, and much read. Dark leather and brass, edges gone dark from handling, writing worked into every surface the use has left free.
entries.comment: The tower's shelf holds the grimoire and extant documents. The grimoire is a folio of names with no title tooled anywhere on it.

entries.value: The tower sits outside all three registers: vocabulary (reads only, cannot invent a rod), capability (grants nothing, not a school), standing (writes nothing to the hollis ledger). It is a site with none — a fifth register would let it start granting things.
entries.comment: The tower deliberately sits outside all three registers. It reads vocabulary, grants nothing, writes nothing.
